Killing of Lord Louis Mountbatten, cousin of Queen Elizabeth II, by a bomb on his fishing boat at Mullaghmore, County Sligo, in the Republic of Ireland, on 27 August 1979.

Mountbatten, 79, was the last viceroy of India and an uncle of Prince Philip. He holidayed at Mullaghmore each summer. The Provisional IRA planted a radio-controlled bomb on his boat Shadow V. It killed him, his 14-year-old grandson Nicholas, and a local boy, Paul Maxwell, 15. His son-in-law's mother, the Dowager Lady Brabourne, died the next day.

The IRA said it wanted to draw the world's attention to the British presence in Ireland. Instead the killing was widely condemned, and Margaret Thatcher's government hardened its stance. On the same day the IRA killed 18 soldiers at the Warrenpoint ambush. Both are part of the-troubles.
sum: Killing of Lord Louis Mountbatten, cousin of Queen Elizabeth II, by a bomb on his fishing boat at Mullaghmore, County Sligo, in the Republic of Ireland, on 27 August 1979.
